title: Interaction-mediated Co-existence of Altermagnetism and Topology
authors: Jasmin Bedow, Nitin Kaushal, Marcel Franz
abstract: We study an extended Hubbard model on Lieb lattice at electron filling 2 and 4, and demonstrate that the interactions lead to the simultaneous emergence of altermagnetic order and a topological gap. Using unrestricted Hartree-Fock theory, we evaluate both the altermagnetic and topological order parameters and show that they co-exist with an associated quantum spin Hall effect in a large region of the phase diagram, which we further support using exact diagonalization. Moreover, we demonstrate that inversion-symmetry breaking terms can also mediate second-order topological phases with associated corner modes.
summary: This paper analyzes an extended Hubbard model on a Lieb lattice to show that electron-electron interactions can spontaneously generate both altermagnetic order and topological gaps. Using Hartree-Fock theory, the authors map out a phase diagram revealing a sequence of correlated insulating and semimetallic states, including a novel TACI phase. This work highlights how strong correlations can mediate the co-existence of magnetism and topology.
main_problem: The study investigates the simultaneous emergence and co-existence of altermagnetic order and a topological gap in interacting electron systems.
main_result: The authors demonstrate that electron-electron interactions naturally drive the system into a Topological Altermagnetic Correlated Insulator (TACI) phase, characterized by both magnetic and topological order.
method: The research employs Unrestricted Hartree-Fock theory to self-consistently evaluate order parameters, supplemented by exact diagonalization for confirmation.
model_or_system: The physical system modeled is an extended Hubbard model defined on a Lieb lattice, incorporating nearest-neighbor and third-neighbor Coulomb interactions.
key_observables: Altermagnetic order (staggered magnetization), topological order (spin Chern number), and the presence of gapless Dirac cones or insulating gaps.
important_parameters: Electron fillings of 2 and 4, and interaction strengths ($U, V$) relative to hopping parameters ($t_1, t_2, t_3$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the Hartree-Fock approximation, and it assumes the A sublattice remains non-magnetic.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the phase diagram mapping the transition between Paramagnetic Metal, Topological Non-Magnetic Insulator (TNM), TACI phase, ALM semimetal, and Mott Insulator as interaction strengths are varied.
paper_structure: The paper systematically maps the phase diagram by increasing interaction strengths, showing a sequence of transitions from a paramagnetic metal to various correlated insulating or semimetallic states.
why_interesting: The explicit coupling between magnetic order (altermagnetism) and topological invariants (Chern number) in a strongly correlated lattice model provides a rich platform for studying emergent quantum phases beyond standard band theory.
